sentences: `D = S0 * S1 + S2` on the low 16-bit halves (VOP3 only).
The product and sum are formed in 32 bits, so nothing overflows, and the low 16 bits are the result.

`op_sel` bits 0..2 read the high half of a source and bit 3 writes the high half of the destination; like the other opsel-capable 16-bit VOP3 ops the other half of the destination is kept (see *16-bit results*).
`clamp` saturates the full-width result to [0, 65535] (`v_mad_u16`) or [-32768, 32767] (`v_mad_i16`).

Source: the AMD [RDNA 2 ISA reference](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/radeon-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/rdna2-shader-instruction-set-architecture.pdf) pseudocode and Mesa ACO's `can_use_opsel`.

Checked on the CPU by `tests/semantic/test_alu_mad_u16_i16.py`; **hardware-verified on RDNA2** (`gfx1035`, wave32 and wave64 via `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both`, SHADER-137): full-width `clamp`, `op_sel` and the untouched destination half match bit-for-bit.
Not run on the shader corpus.
